claim: For the Moysis–Volos cubic–absolute-value flow \(\dot x=yz\), \(\dot y=x^3-y^3\), \(\dot z=a|x|-by^3-xy\) with \(a,b>0\), the equilibrium set consists of the full line \(\{(0,0,z)\}\) plus an isolated positive equilibrium for every parameter pair and, when \(0<4ab<1\), two additional isolated negative equilibria (coalescing at \(4ab=1\)). At any isolated equilibrium \(E_r=(r,r,0)\), the characteristic polynomial is \(\lambda^3+3r^2\lambda^2-br^3\lambda+3r^4(1+2br)\). The positive branch has two right-half-plane eigenvalues; the more-negative branch has one; the less-negative branch is asymptotically stable exactly for \(2/9<ab<1/4\), has a negative eigenvalue and a purely imaginary pair at \(ab=2/9\), and is unstable for \(0<ab<2/9\). For the published example \(a=0.65\), \(b=0.1\), there are three omitted isolated equilibria and all are unstable. Hence the published statement that all equilibria lie on \((0,0,z)\) is false, and hiddenness cannot be inferred from that line-only equilibrium argument without checking basin behavior near the omitted equilibria.

correctness.rationale: Direct real-algebra elimination gives the complete equilibrium set. At each isolated root the absolute value is smooth; the exact Jacobian reduces, using the equilibrium relation, to the stated cubic characteristic polynomial. Routh–Hurwitz gives the right-half-plane counts and the stable interval \(2/9<ab<1/4\). The critical factorization and source-parameter roots were replayed symbolically from the packaged script.

value.rationale: The source uses its claimed line equilibrium as a structural reason for hidden-attractor status. Correcting that equilibrium set is therefore not a cosmetic algebra check: it adds isolated equilibria for every positive parameter pair, a full parameter-dependent equilibrium count, and an exact stability partition, all directly relevant to basin-based attractor classification. The claim remains conservative by not asserting self-excitedness without a basin proof.
